transcript.text: Good morning everyone. As we all know, we have one two-hour MRI slot tomorrow from 1:00 PM to 3:00 PM, and both Patient Avery and Patient Morgan are currently listed for consideration. I'll be making the final imaging plan, but before I finalize anything, I need to run through our routine pre-release process — checking with neuroradiology, the MRI technologist, utilization review, and patient access. I'd like to get that process started now so we can make the best decision for that slot. Could I get input from each of those areas regarding both patients?
transcript.speaker: A1

transcript.text: I need to flag something urgent regarding Patient Avery. Avery developed a new focal neurologic deficit this morning, and the treating physician wants a brain MRI with and without contrast completed before a treatment decision at 2:00 PM tomorrow. I reviewed the clinical message, but the updated urgency and protocol are not yet in the scheduling record. This is time-sensitive — the treatment decision at 2:00 PM falls right in the middle of our available slot, so we need to account for this.
transcript.speaker: A2

transcript.text: I need to flag a critical safety issue regarding Patient Morgan. Morgan has an implanted neurostimulator that is approved for MRI only on a 1.5-tesla system with a dedicated transmit-receive head coil. Our hospital scanner for tomorrow's slot is a 3-tesla system, so Morgan cannot safely be scanned here. Morgan must be referred to Lakeside Imaging's 1.5-tesla scanner instead of being placed in this slot.
transcript.speaker: A3

transcript.text: Regarding Patient Avery, I have important utilization review information. Avery's insurer authorization is already approved specifically for a brain MRI with and without contrast at the hospital outpatient imaging department. I have the authorization number in the utilization portal, but it has not yet been attached to the scheduling encounter. This means Avery is already authorized for exactly the type of scan Dr. Chen is describing, at our hospital — so from a utilization review standpoint, Avery is cleared for tomorrow's hospital MRI slot.
